questionText: What should our city do to improve residents' quality of life?
design: Gemini-authored accuracy corpus: 10 topics x 5 synth-groups x 2 near-paraphrases = 100 statements. Pairs are same-action rewordings; groups within a topic are distinct interventions; topics are distinct domains.

synths.name: frequent-peak-buses
paraphrases: Run buses more often during morning and evening rush hours.
Increase the frequency of transit service when people are commuting to and from work.

synths.name: weekend-night-service
paraphrases: Add late-night bus routes on Friday and Saturday.
Keep public transit running after midnight on the weekends.

synths.name: free-student-transit
paraphrases: Make all city buses free for students under eighteen.
Don't charge middle and high schoolers to ride the bus.

synths.name: dedicated-bus-lanes
paraphrases: Install dedicated transit corridors on all major arterial roads.
Paint red bus-only lanes on the biggest avenues so they don't get stuck in traffic.

synths.name: bus-stop-shelters
paraphrases: Build roofs and benches at every bus stop in the city.
Ensure waiting areas for riders have seating and protection from the rain.

synths.name: rent-control
paraphrases: Cap the amount landlords can raise rent each year.
Pass a law limiting annual rent increases for tenants.

synths.name: missing-middle-zoning
paraphrases: Change zoning laws to allow missing-middle housing everywhere.
Let developers build duplexes, triplexes, and townhomes in neighborhoods that are currently just single-family.

synths.name: vacant-property-tax
paraphrases: Charge a high fee to owners who leave residential properties empty.
Tax absentee landlords who keep houses vacant instead of renting them out.

synths.name: first-time-buyer-grants
paraphrases: Provide city grants to help first-time buyers with their down payments.
Offer financial assistance to working families trying to purchase their first home.

synths.name: expedite-affordable-permits
paraphrases: Fast-track the permitting process for affordable housing projects.
Move construction applications for low-income apartments to the very front of the line.

synths.name: enclosed-dog-parks
paraphrases: Build enclosed off-leash dog areas in every neighborhood.
Create fenced-in spaces where people can let their pets run freely.

synths.name: late-park-hours
paraphrases: Keep the main city parks open and lit until midnight.
Extend the hours of our public green spaces so people can use them after dark.

synths.name: vacant-lot-gardens
paraphrases: Turn vacant city lots into plots where neighbors can grow their own food.
Convert unused public land into community gardens for local residents.

synths.name: downtown-splash-pads
paraphrases: Install aquatic recreation features for children in the major plazas.
Put in splash pads and interactive fountains downtown so kids can cool off.

synths.name: paved-river-trails
paraphrases: Pave the dirt walking paths along the river so they don't get muddy.
Lay down concrete on the riverside trails to make them accessible year-round.

synths.name: curbside-compost
paraphrases: Start a citywide curbside pickup program for food scraps.
Collect organic waste from houses every week alongside the regular trash.

synths.name: public-receptacles
paraphrases: Place waste receptacles at high-traffic pedestrian intersections.
Put trash cans and recycling bins on every busy street corner.

synths.name: ban-single-use-plastics
paraphrases: Make it illegal for stores and restaurants to hand out single-use plastics.
Ban the distribution of disposable grocery bags and plastic straws at local businesses.

synths.name: e-waste-dropoff
paraphrases: Host a monthly event where people can safely get rid of old electronics.
Set up a regular drop-off site for broken computers and televisions.

synths.name: littering-fines
paraphrases: Increase the financial penalties for people caught littering on the sidewalks.
Hand out much bigger tickets to anyone throwing garbage on the ground.

synths.name: municipal-broadband
paraphrases: Create a city-owned internet service to compete with private monopolies.
Build a public broadband network so we aren't forced to use the big telecom companies.

synths.name: downtown-wifi
paraphrases: Deploy outdoor public connectivity infrastructure in the commercial district.
Set up free municipal Wi-Fi access points all along Main Street and the town square.

synths.name: library-hotspots
paraphrases: Allow residents to check out portable internet hotspots from the public library.
Let library card holders borrow mobile routers to get online at home.

synths.name: senior-digital-literacy
paraphrases: Offer free evening classes to teach seniors how to use modern technology.
Host workshops at the community center helping older folks navigate smartphones and computers.

synths.name: unified-city-app
paraphrases: Develop a single mobile app for reporting potholes and paying utility bills.
Make a central smartphone program where citizens can handle all their city business at once.

synths.name: school-traffic-calming
paraphrases: Implement physical traffic-calming measures in residential school zones.
Install speed bumps, raised crosswalks, and narrowed lanes right next to the elementary schools.

synths.name: led-streetlights
paraphrases: Upgrade all the neighborhood streetlights to brighter LED bulbs.
Replace the dim yellow street lamps with bright white lights to make sidewalks safer.

synths.name: mental-health-response
paraphrases: Send social workers instead of armed police to mental health emergency calls.
Dispatch unarmed behavioral health specialists to deal with people in crisis.

synths.name: school-crossing-guards
paraphrases: Hire adults to manage traffic for children walking to every school.
Pay crossing guards to stand at busy intersections near schools during drop-off and pickup.

synths.name: garage-security-cameras
paraphrases: Put security cameras in all the city-owned parking structures.
Install video surveillance inside the municipal parking decks to deter break-ins.

synths.name: small-business-grants
paraphrases: Give startup grants to residents opening their first storefront.
Provide direct funding to locals who want to launch a brick-and-mortar business.

synths.name: pedestrian-main-street
paraphrases: Remove vehicular access from the primary downtown retail corridor.
Block off Main Street to cars entirely so people can safely walk between shops and restaurants.

synths.name: buy-local-campaign
paraphrases: Fund an advertising campaign encouraging people to shop at independent local stores.
Run city-sponsored ads reminding folks to spend their money at locally owned businesses.

synths.name: streamline-licenses
paraphrases: Reduce the paperwork required to get a new commercial license.
Make the application process for opening a restaurant much shorter and easier.

synths.name: food-truck-zones
paraphrases: Designate specific parking areas downtown exclusively for mobile food vendors.
Create a dedicated zone where food trucks can park and operate every single day.

synths.name: pothole-repair-guarantee
paraphrases: Commit to filling reported potholes within forty-eight hours.
Guarantee that road craters will be patched within two days of a resident calling them in.

synths.name: protected-bike-lanes
paraphrases: Install physical separation infrastructure between cyclists and motor vehicles.
Put up concrete barriers and plastic bollards to keep cars out of the bike lanes.

synths.name: permeable-pavement
paraphrases: Require new parking lots to use surfaces that let rain soak through.
Mandate permeable asphalt or paving stones for commercial lots to reduce flooding.

synths.name: priority-snow-plowing
paraphrases: Plow the streets leading to hospitals and fire stations before anything else.
Clear the snow off emergency routes immediately after a storm hits.

synths.name: repaint-crosswalks
paraphrases: Repaint the faded pedestrian crosswalks at every major intersection.
Put a fresh coat of white paint on all the crosswalk lines so drivers can actually see them.

synths.name: municipal-solar
paraphrases: Install solar panels on the roofs of all government-owned facilities.
Put photovoltaic arrays on the library, city hall, and the community centers.

synths.name: public-ev-chargers
paraphrases: Expand electric vehicle charging infrastructure in public lots.
Install Level 2 chargers and DC fast chargers in all the municipal parking garages.

synths.name: tree-canopy-expansion
paraphrases: Plant a thousand new native trees in low-income neighborhoods this year.
Add a massive amount of shade trees to the poorest parts of the city.

synths.name: home-insulation-subsidies
paraphrases: Help homeowners pay for better weatherization and insulation.
Offer rebates to residents who upgrade their windows and seal drafts in their houses.

synths.name: ban-gas-leaf-blowers
paraphrases: Make it illegal for landscaping companies to use noisy, gas-powered leaf blowers.
Prohibit the use of two-stroke engine leaf blowers within city limits.

synths.name: public-murals
paraphrases: Commission large-scale visual artworks on blank commercial facades.
Pay local painters to create huge colorful murals on the boring sides of downtown buildings.

synths.name: street-music-festival
paraphrases: Organize an annual weekend festival focused on local bands and street musicians.
Host a yearly music event downtown highlighting artists who live in the city.

synths.name: subsidized-artist-studios
paraphrases: Convert empty warehouses into cheap rental studios for working artists.
Turn abandoned industrial buildings into affordable workspaces for painters and sculptors.

synths.name: free-museum-days
paraphrases: Require city-funded museums to offer free admission one day a week.
Make the local art and history institutions waive ticket fees every Tuesday.

synths.name: block-party-permits
paraphrases: Waive the street closure fees for neighborhoods throwing summer block parties.
Stop charging residents for the permits they need to close their street for a community cookout.
